Tomato___healthy.title: Routine Crop Scouting
Tomato___healthy.description: Inspect 20 random plants weekly across the field, especially lower leaves and leaf undersides, for early pest or disease symptoms.

Tomato___healthy.title: Drip Irrigation Management
Tomato___healthy.description: Maintain uniform soil moisture at the root zone via drip lines; avoid wetting the foliage to discourage fungal spore germination.

Tomato___healthy.title: Soil Organic Enrichment
Tomato___healthy.description: Incorporate well-decomposed farmyard manure (FYM) or vermicompost to promote beneficial soil microbiome diversity.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Lower Canopy Pruning & Sanitation
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Prune and destroy infected lower leaves up to 12 inches above the soil line to eliminate splash inoculation sources.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Bio-control with Trichoderma / Pseudomonas
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Foliar spray with Trichoderma harzianum or Pseudomonas fluorescens culture early morning to colonize leaf surfaces and outcompete fungal spores.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Organic Mulching
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Apply a 2-inch layer of clean paddy straw or plastic mulch around the plant base to prevent rain and irrigation droplets splashing soil spores onto leaves.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Crop Rotation Cycle
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops (maize, legumes, crucifers) for at least 2 to 3 years to starve fungal resting spores in soil.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.title: Hot Water Seed Treatment
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Soak seed in water at 50°C for 25 minutes prior to nursery sowing to eradicate seed-borne bacterial inoculum.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.title: Biological Antagonist Application
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens or Bacillus subtilis cell suspension to competitively displace bacterial pathogens on leaves.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.title: Avoid Handling Wet Plants
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Never prune, stake, or harvest while leaves are wet with rain or morning dew, as bacterial droplets spread readily on tools and hands.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.title: Airflow & Staking
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Stake plants properly and maintain 60 cm between rows to accelerate leaf canopy drying after rain.

Tomato___Late_blight.title: Immediate Eradication of Infected Foliage
Tomato___Late_blight.description: Bag and deeply bury or burn severely blighted leaves and infected vines immediately. Do not add infected residue to compost piles.

Tomato___Late_blight.title: Trichoderma Soil & Foliar Bio-shield
Tomato___Late_blight.description: Apply Trichoderma viride enriched FYM to the root zone and spray bio-fungicide formulations during cool, damp weather to inhibit oomycete sporulation.

Tomato___Late_blight.title: Strict Furrow/Drip Irrigation
Tomato___Late_blight.description: Never use overhead sprinklers. Irrigate early in the morning so sun quickly evaporates any accidental moisture from lower stems.

Tomato___Late_blight.title: Elimination of Volunteer Solanaceous Hosts
Tomato___Late_blight.description: Destroy volunteer tomato, potato, and weed nightshades around field margins that act as overwintering infection reservoirs.

Cabbage___healthy.title: Regular Moisture Maintenance
Cabbage___healthy.description: Maintain even soil moisture to avoid split cabbage heads and prevent moisture stress.

Cabbage___healthy.title: Beneficial Soil Organic Matter
Cabbage___healthy.description: Apply composted neem cake or vermicompost to fortify soil with nutrients and natural pest repellency.

Cabbage___healthy.title: Weekly Scouting for Pests
Cabbage___healthy.description: Inspect inner leaves and head whorls for early signs of diamondback moth caterpillars or aphids.

Tomato___Spider_mites.title: Neem Oil / Azadirachtin Spray
Tomato___Spider_mites.description: Apply cold-pressed neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) or botanical neem oil targeting the leaf undersides where mites feed and lay eggs.

Tomato___Spider_mites.title: Biological Predatory Mites
Tomato___Spider_mites.description: Encourage or release native predatory mites (e.g., Phytoseiidae species) and ladybird beetles (Stethorus) that actively consume spider mites.

Tomato___Spider_mites.title: High-Pressure Water Spray
Tomato___Spider_mites.description: Direct a firm stream of clean water to the underside of leaves during morning hours to physically disrupt webbing and dislodge mites.

Tomato___Spider_mites.title: Dust & Border Weed Control
Tomato___Spider_mites.description: Wet farm access paths to reduce airborne dust (which promotes mite outbreaks) and remove wild weed hosts from bunds.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.title: High Ventilation & Defoliation
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Remove lower older leaves and suckers up to the first fruit cluster to promote strong horizontal air currents through the crop canopy.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.title: Biological Bio-fungicide Application
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Apply Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma harzianum bio-agent sprays to suppress mycelial development on lower leaf surfaces.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.title: Relative Humidity Reduction
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: In polyhouse or sheltered conditions, maintain humidity below 85% by opening side curtains and ensuring good ground drainage.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Strict Eradication of Infected Plants (Rogueing)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Uproot viral-symptomatic plants into sealed bags as soon as observed and destroy them to prevent whiteflies acquiring and spreading virus.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Yellow Sticky Traps for Vector Monitoring
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Install 15-20 bright yellow sticky traps per acre just above crop canopy height to capture and monitor adult whitefly populations.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Insect Exclusion Nursery Netting
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Raise seedlings under 40-50 mesh insect-proof nylon net tunnels to prevent viruliferous whiteflies infesting young nursery plants.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Neem-Based Whitefly Repellent
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Spray 1% neem oil or NSKE extract to repel whiteflies and inhibit egg hatching on tender top foliage.

Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.title: Deep Summer Tillage
Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.description: Incorporate and deeply bury previous crop stubble to accelerate decomposition of fungal stromata before the new growing season.

Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.title: Trichoderma Seed Inoculation
Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.description: Treat soybean seeds with Trichoderma viride dry powder formulation along with Rhizobium inoculant before sowing.

Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.title: 2-Year Crop Rotation
Soybean___Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.description: Rotate soybean fields with corn, sorghum, or small grain cereals for two consecutive seasons to disrupt the pathogen cycle.

Soybean___Downy_Mildew.title: Plant Density Optimization
Soybean___Downy_Mildew.description: Avoid excessive seed rates; maintain 45 cm row spacing to facilitate sun penetration and rapid morning dew evaporation.

Soybean___Downy_Mildew.title: Biological Seed Coating
Soybean___Downy_Mildew.description: Inoculate certified seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-formulation to protect early seedling emergence from oospore infection.

Soybean___Downy_Mildew.title: Clean Field Sanitation
Soybean___Downy_Mildew.description: Destroy volunteer soybean seedlings and infected haulms remaining in the field post-harvest.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.title: Early Planting Schedule
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Sow maize crops early in the season to ensure grain filling finishes before peak cool, humid conditions favor rust development.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.title: Balanced Nutrient Management
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Avoid excessive nitrogen application which produces succulent, rust-susceptible tissues; apply adequate potassium to strengthen cell walls.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.title: Trichoderma Soil Application
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Incorporate Trichoderma-fortified compost during basal soil preparation to stimulate systemic induced plant defense mechanisms.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.title: Optimal Soil Aeration & Moisture
Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Ensure good drainage during flowering and grain fill; avoid both water-logging and severe moisture deficit.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.title: Routine Vegetative Scouting
Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Check top and bottom leaves every two weeks for signs of stem borers, armyworms, or foliar leaf spots.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.title: Crop Residue Management
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Chop and bury corn stalks after harvest to speed microbial breakdown of fungal debris living in surface residues.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.title: Non-Host Crop Rotation
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Alternate corn with soybean, groundnut, or pigeon pea for two seasons; Cercospora cannot survive on dicotyledonous crops.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.title: Canopy Airflow Enhancement
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Maintain recommended plant populations (around 24,000 plants per acre) to prevent prolonged humidity inside the canopy.

Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis.title: Complete Rogueing & Quarantine
Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis.description: Immediately pull out and burn any maize plants showing mottled chlorosis or dead hearts to prevent vector spread.

Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis.title: Strict Crop-Free Break Period
Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis.description: Observe at least a 2-month maize-free period across the community to break the lifecycle of insect vectors (thrips and chrysomelids).

Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis.title: Non-Grass Crop Diversification
Corn_(maize)___Lethal_Necrosis.description: Rotate fields strictly with legumes, sunflower, or cotton; avoid planting near sorghum, sugarcane, or wild grass borders.

Soybean___healthy.title: Rhizobium Bio-fertilizer Management
Soybean___healthy.description: Ensure optimal nodulation by maintaining neutral soil pH and avoiding unnecessary synthetic nitrogen overload.

Soybean___healthy.title: Routine Field Monitoring
Soybean___healthy.description: Inspect leaf whorls and pod clusters during flowering and pod development for early signs of defoliation or blight.

Cabbage___Black_Rot.title: Hot Water Seed Disinfestation
Cabbage___Black_Rot.description: Immerse cabbage seed in hot water at precisely 50°C for 30 minutes, followed by rapid cooling, to kill seed-borne Xanthomonas bacteria.

Cabbage___Black_Rot.title: 3-Year Crucifer-Free Rotation
Cabbage___Black_Rot.description: Never plant cabbage, cauliflower, mustard, or radish on the same land for 3 years; rotate with corn, legumes, or solanaceous crops.

Cabbage___Black_Rot.title: Elimination of Wild Cruciferous Weeds
Cabbage___Black_Rot.description: Eradicate wild mustard, shepherd's purse, and radish weeds along field boundaries that harbor and multiply the bacterial pathogen.

Cabbage___Black_Rot.title: Drip Irrigation
Cabbage___Black_Rot.description: Irrigate strictly via drip lines at ground level; overhead splashing spreads bacterial droplets across leaves rapidly.
